NKJV.1: Saul reigned one year; and when he had reigned two years over Israel,
NKJV.2: Saul chose for himself three thousand men of Israel. Two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and in the mountains of Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin. The rest of the people he sent away, every man to his tent.
NKJV.3: And Jonathan attacked the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. Then Saul blew the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, “Let the Hebrews hear!”
NKJV.4: Now all Israel heard it said that Saul had attacked a garrison of the Philistines, and that Israel had also become an abomination to the Philistines. And the people were called together to Saul at Gilgal.
NKJV.5: Then the Philistines gathered together to fight with Israel, thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen, and people as the sand which is on the seashore in multitude. And they came up and encamped in Michmash, to the east of Beth Aven.
NKJV.6: When the men of Israel saw that they were in danger (for the people were distressed), then the people hid in caves, in thickets, in rocks, in holes, and in pits.
NKJV.7: And some of the Hebrews crossed over the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead. As for Saul, he was still in Gilgal, and all the people followed him trembling.
NKJV.8: Then he waited seven days, according to the time set by Samuel. But Samuel did not come to Gilgal; and the people were scattered from him.
NKJV.9: So Saul said, “Bring a burnt offering and peace offerings here to me.” And he offered the burnt offering.
NKJV.10: Now it happened, as soon as he had finished presenting the burnt offering, that Samuel came; and Saul went out to meet him, that he might greet him.
NKJV.11: And Samuel said, “What have you done?” Saul said, “When I saw that the people were scattered from me, and that you did not come within the days appointed, and that the Philistines gathered together at Michmash,
NKJV.12: then I said, ‘The Philistines will now come down on me at Gilgal, and I have not made supplication to the LORD.’ Therefore I felt compelled, and offered a burnt offering.”
NKJV.13: And Samuel said to Saul, “You have done foolishly. You have not kept the commandment of the LORD your God, which He commanded you. For now the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel forever.
NKJV.14: But now your kingdom shall not continue. The LORD has sought for Himself a man after His own heart, and the LORD has commanded him to be commander over His people, because you have not kept what the LORD commanded you.”
NKJV.15: Then Samuel arose and went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul numbered the people present with him, about six hundred men.
NKJV.16: Saul, Jonathan his son, and the people present with them remained in Gibeah of Benjamin. But the Philistines encamped in Michmash.
NKJV.17: Then raiders came out of the camp of the Philistines in three companies. One company turned onto the road to Ophrah, to the land of Shual,
NKJV.18: another company turned to the road to Beth Horon, and another company turned to the road of the border that overlooks the Valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness.
NKJV.19: Now there was no blacksmith to be found throughout all the land of Israel, for the Philistines said, “Lest the Hebrews make swords or spears.”
NKJV.20: But all the Israelites would go down to the Philistines to sharpen each man’s plowshare, his mattock, his ax, and his sickle;
NKJV.21: and the charge for a sharpening was a pim for the plowshares, the mattocks, the forks, and the axes, and to set the points of the goads.
NKJV.22: So it came about, on the day of battle, that there was neither sword nor spear found in the hand of any of the people who were with Saul and Jonathan. But they were found with Saul and Jonathan his son.
NKJV.23: And the garrison of the Philistines went out to the pass of Michmash.

ESV.1: Saul lived for one year and then became king, and when he had reigned for two years over Israel,
ESV.2: Saul chose three thousand men of Israel. Two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and the hill country of Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin. The rest of the people he sent home, every man to his tent.
ESV.3: Jonathan defeated the garrison of the Philistines that was at Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. And Saul blew the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, “Let the Hebrews hear.”
ESV.4: And all Israel heard it said that Saul had defeated the garrison of the Philistines, and also that Israel had become a stench to the Philistines. And the people were called out to join Saul at Gilgal.
ESV.5: And the Philistines mustered to fight with Israel, thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen and troops like the sand on the seashore in multitude. They came up and encamped in Michmash, to the east of Beth-aven.
ESV.6: When the men of Israel saw that they were in trouble (for the people were hard pressed), the people hid themselves in caves and in holes and in rocks and in tombs and in cisterns,
ESV.7: and some Hebrews crossed the fords of the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead. Saul was still at Gilgal, and all the people followed him trembling.
ESV.8: He waited seven days, the time appointed by Samuel. But Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the people were scattering from him.
ESV.9: So Saul said, “Bring the burnt offering here to me, and the peace offerings.” And he offered the burnt offering.
ESV.10: As soon as he had finished offering the burnt offering, behold, Samuel came. And Saul went out to meet him and greet him.
ESV.11: Samuel said, “What have you done?” And Saul said, “When I saw that the people were scattering from me, and that you did not come within the days appointed, and that the Philistines had mustered at Michmash,
ESV.12: I said, ‘Now the Philistines will come down against me at Gilgal, and I have not sought the favor of the LORD.’ So I forced myself, and offered the burnt offering.”
ESV.13: And Samuel said to Saul, “You have done foolishly. You have not kept the command of the LORD your God, with which he commanded you. For then the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel forever.
ESV.14: But now your kingdom shall not continue. The LORD has sought out a man after his own heart, and the LORD has commanded him to be prince  over his people, because you have not kept what the LORD commanded you.”
ESV.15: And Samuel arose and went up from Gilgal. The rest of the people went up after Saul to meet the army; they went up from Gilgal  to Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul numbered the people who were present with him, about six hundred men.
ESV.16: And Saul and Jonathan his son and the people who were present with them stayed in Geba of Benjamin, but the Philistines encamped in Michmash.
ESV.17: And raiders came out of the camp of the Philistines in three companies. One company turned toward Ophrah, to the land of Shual;
ESV.18: another company turned toward Beth-horon; and another company turned toward the border that looks down on the Valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness.
ESV.19: Now there was no blacksmith to be found throughout all the land of Israel, for the Philistines said, “Lest the Hebrews make themselves swords or spears.”
ESV.20: But every one of the Israelites went down to the Philistines to sharpen his plowshare, his mattock, his axe, or his sickle,
ESV.21: and the charge was two-thirds of a shekel  for the plowshares and for the mattocks, and a third of a shekel  for sharpening the axes and for setting the goads.
ESV.22: So on the day of the battle there was neither sword nor spear found in the hand of any of the people with Saul and Jonathan, but Saul and Jonathan his son had them.
ESV.23: And the garrison of the Philistines went out to the pass of Michmash.

NASB.1: Saul was [thirty] years old when he began to reign, and he reigned [forty] two years over Israel.
NASB.2: Now Saul chose for himself 3,000 men of Israel, of which 2,000 were with Saul in Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel, while 1,000 were with Jonathan at Gibeah of Benjamin. But he sent away the rest of the people, each to his tent.
NASB.3: Jonathan smote the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba, and the Philistines heard of [it]. Then Saul blew the trumpet throughout the land, saying, 'Let the Hebrews hear.'
NASB.4: All Israel heard the news that Saul had smitten the garrison of the Philistines, and also that Israel had become odious to the Philistines. The people were then summoned to Saul at Gilgal.
NASB.5: Now the Philistines assembled to fight with Israel, 30,000 chariots and 6,000 horsemen, and people like the sand which is on the seashore in abundance; and they came up and camped in Michmash, east of Beth-aven.
NASB.6: When the men of Israel saw that they were in a strait (for the people were hard-pressed), then the people hid themselves in caves, in thickets, in cliffs, in cellars, and in pits.
NASB.7: Also [some of] the Hebrews crossed the Jordan into the land of Gad and Gilead. But as for Saul, he [was] still in Gilgal, and all the people followed him trembling.
NASB.8: Now he waited seven days, according to the appointed time set by Samuel, but Samuel did not come to Gilgal; and the people were scattering from him.
NASB.9: So Saul said, 'Bring to me the burnt offering and the peace offerings.' And he offered the burnt offering.
NASB.10: As soon as he finished offering the burnt offering, behold, Samuel came; and Saul went out to meet him [and] to greet him.
NASB.11: But Samuel said, 'What have you done?' And Saul said, 'Because I saw that the people were scattering from me, and that you did not come within the appointed days, and that the Philistines were assembling at Michmash,
NASB.12: therefore I said, 'Now the Philistines will come down against me at Gilgal, and I have not asked the favor of the LORD.' So I forced myself and offered the burnt offering.'
NASB.13: Samuel said to Saul, 'You have acted foolishly; you have not kept the commandment of the LORD your God, which He commanded you, for now the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel forever.
NASB.14: 'But now your kingdom shall not endure. The LORD has sought out for Himself a man after His own heart, and the LORD has appointed him as ruler over His people, because you have not kept what the LORD commanded you.'
NASB.15: Then Samuel arose and went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul numbered the people who were present with him, about six hundred men.
NASB.16: Now Saul and his son Jonathan and the people who were present with them were staying in Geba of Benjamin while the Philistines camped at Michmash.
NASB.17: And the raiders came from the camp of the Philistines in three companies: one company turned toward Ophrah, to the land of Shual,
NASB.18: and another company turned toward Beth-horon, and another company turned toward the border which overlooks the valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness.
NASB.19: Now no blacksmith could be found in all the land of Israel, for the Philistines said, 'Otherwise the Hebrews will make swords or spears.'
NASB.20: So all Israel went down to the Philistines, each to sharpen his plowshare, his mattock, his axe, and his hoe.
NASB.21: The charge was two-thirds of a shekel for the plowshares, the mattocks, the forks, and the axes, and to fix the hoes.
NASB.22: So it came about on the day of battle that neither sword nor spear was found in the hands of any of the people who [were] with Saul and Jonathan, but they were found with Saul and his son Jonathan.
NASB.23: And the garrison of the Philistines went out to the pass of Michmash.

CSB17.1: Saul was thirty years <sup>[1]</sup> old when he became king, and he reigned forty-two years <sup>[2]</sup> over Israel. <sup>[3]</sup>
CSB17.2: He chose three thousand men from Israel for himself: two thousand were with Saul at Michmash <sup>ⓚ</sup> and in Bethel’s hill country, and one thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah <sup>ⓛ</sup> of Benjamin. He sent the rest of the troops away, each to his own tent.
CSB17.3: Jonathan attacked the Philistine garrison <sup>[4]</sup> <sup>ⓜ</sup> that was in Geba, <sup>ⓝ</sup> and the Philistines heard about it. So Saul blew the ram’s horn throughout the land <sup>ⓐ</sup> saying, “Let the Hebrews hear!” <sup>[5]</sup> <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.4: And all Israel heard the news, “Saul has attacked the Philistine garrison, and Israel is now repulsive to the Philistines.” Then the troops were summoned to join Saul at Gilgal.
CSB17.5: The Philistines also gathered to fight against Israel: three thousand <sup>[6]</sup> chariots, six thousand horsemen, and troops as numerous as the sand on the seashore. <sup>ⓒ</sup> They went up and camped at Michmash, east of Beth-aven. <sup>[7]</sup> <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.6: The men of Israel saw that they were in trouble because the troops were in a difficult situation. They hid in caves, in thickets, among rocks, and in holes and cisterns. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.7: Some Hebrews even crossed the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead. Saul, however, was still at Gilgal, and all his troops were gripped with fear.
CSB17.8: He waited seven days for the appointed time that Samuel had set, <sup>ⓕ</sup> but Samuel didn’t come to Gilgal, and the troops were deserting him.
CSB17.9: So Saul said, “Bring me the burnt offering and the fellowship offerings.” Then he offered the burnt offering.
CSB17.10: Just as he finished offering the burnt offering, Samuel arrived. So Saul went out to greet him,
CSB17.11: and Samuel asked, “What have you done?” Saul answered, “When I saw that the troops were deserting me and you didn’t come within the appointed days and the Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
CSB17.12: I thought, ‘The Philistines will now descend on me at Gilgal, and I haven’t sought the LORD’s favor.’ So I forced myself to offer the burnt offering.”
CSB17.13: Samuel said to Saul, “You have been foolish. <sup>ⓖ</sup> You have not kept the command the LORD your God gave you. <sup>ⓗ</sup> It was at this time that the LORD would have permanently established your reign over Israel, <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.14: but now your reign will not endure. <sup>ⓙ</sup> The LORD has found a man after his own heart, <sup>[8]</sup> <sup>ⓚ</sup> and the LORD has appointed him as ruler over his people, because you have not done what the LORD commanded.”
CSB17.15: Then Samuel went <sup>[9]</sup> from Gilgal to Gibeah in Benjamin. Saul registered the troops who were with him, about six hundred men.
CSB17.16: Saul, his son Jonathan, and the troops who were with them were staying in Geba <sup>ⓛ</sup> of Benjamin, and the Philistines were camped at Michmash.
CSB17.17: Raiding parties <sup>ⓜ</sup> went out from the Philistine camp in three divisions. One division headed toward the Ophrah <sup>ⓝ</sup> road leading to the land of Shual.
CSB17.18: The next division headed toward the Beth-horon <sup>ⓐ</sup> road, and the last division headed down the border road that looks out over the Zeboim Valley <sup>ⓑ</sup> toward the wilderness.
CSB17.19: No blacksmith could be found in all the land of Israel <sup>ⓒ</sup> because the Philistines had said, “Otherwise, the Hebrews will make swords or spears.”
CSB17.20: So all the Israelites went to the Philistines to sharpen their plows, mattocks, axes, and sickles. <sup>[10]</sup>
CSB17.21: The price was two-thirds of a shekel <sup>[11]</sup> for plows and mattocks, and one-third of a shekel for pitchforks and axes, and for putting a point on a cattle prod.
CSB17.22: So on the day of battle not a sword or spear could be found in the hand of any of the troops who were with Saul <sup>ⓓ</sup> and Jonathan; only Saul and his son Jonathan had weapons.
CSB17.23: Now a Philistine garrison <sup>ⓔ</sup> took control of the pass at Michmash.

NLT.1: Saul was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned for forty-two years.
NLT.2: Saul selected 3,000 special troops from the army of Israel and sent the rest of the men home. He took 2,000 of the chosen men with him to Micmash and the hill country of Bethel. The other 1,000 went with Saul’s son Jonathan to Gibeah in the land of Benjamin.
NLT.3: Soon after this, Jonathan attacked and defeated the garrison of Philistines at Geba. The news spread quickly among the Philistines. So Saul blew the ram’s horn throughout the land, saying, “Hebrews, hear this! Rise up in revolt!”
NLT.4: All Israel heard the news that Saul had destroyed the Philistine garrison at Geba and that the Philistines now hated the Israelites more than ever. So the entire Israelite army was summoned to join Saul at Gilgal.
NLT.5: The Philistines mustered a mighty army of 3,000 chariots, 6,000 charioteers, and as many warriors as the grains of sand on the seashore! They camped at Micmash east of Beth-aven.
NLT.6: The men of Israel saw what a tight spot they were in; and because they were hard pressed by the enemy, they tried to hide in caves, thickets, rocks, holes, and cisterns.
NLT.7: Some of them crossed the Jordan River and escaped into the land of Gad and Gilead. Saul’s Disobedience and Samuel’s Rebuke Meanwhile, Saul stayed at Gilgal, and his men were trembling with fear.
NLT.8: Saul waited there seven days for Samuel, as Samuel had instructed him earlier, but Samuel still didn’t come. Saul realized that his troops were rapidly slipping away.
NLT.9: So he demanded, “Bring me the burnt offering and the peace offerings!” And Saul sacrificed the burnt offering himself.
NLT.10: Just as Saul was finishing with the burnt offering, Samuel arrived. Saul went out to meet and welcome him,
NLT.11: but Samuel said, “What is this you have done?” Saul replied, “I saw my men scattering from me, and you didn’t arrive when you said you would, and the Philistines are at Micmash ready for battle.
NLT.12: So I said, ‘The Philistines are ready to march against us at Gilgal, and I haven’t even asked for the LORD’s help!’ So I felt compelled to offer the burnt offering myself before you came.”
NLT.13: “How foolish!” Samuel exclaimed. “You have not kept the command the LORD your God gave you. Had you kept it, the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel forever.
NLT.14: But now your kingdom must end, for the LORD has sought out a man after his own heart. The LORD has already appointed him to be the leader of his people, because you have not kept the LORD’s command.”
NLT.15: Samuel then left Gilgal and went on his way, but the rest of the troops went with Saul to meet the army. They went up from Gilgal to Gibeah in the land of Benjamin. When Saul counted the men who were still with him, he found only 600 were left!
NLT.16: Saul and Jonathan and the troops with them were staying at Geba in the land of Benjamin. The Philistines set up their camp at Micmash.
NLT.17: Three raiding parties soon left the camp of the Philistines. One went north toward Ophrah in the land of Shual,
NLT.18: another went west to Beth-horon, and the third moved toward the border above the valley of Zeboim near the wilderness.
NLT.19: There were no blacksmiths in the land of Israel in those days. The Philistines wouldn’t allow them for fear they would make swords and spears for the Hebrews.
NLT.20: So whenever the Israelites needed to sharpen their plowshares, picks, axes, or sickles, they had to take them to a Philistine blacksmith.
NLT.21: The charges were as follows: a quarter of an ounce of silver for sharpening a plowshare or a pick, and an eighth of an ounce for sharpening an ax or making the point of an ox goad.
NLT.22: So on the day of the battle none of the people of Israel had a sword or spear, except for Saul and Jonathan.
NLT.23: The pass at Micmash had meanwhile been secured by a contingent of the Philistine army.

WEB.1: Saul was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned over Israel forty-two years.

MSG.1: Saul was a young man when he began as king. He was king over Israel for many years.
MSG.2: Saul conscripted enough men for three companies of soldiers. He kept two companies under his command at Micmash and in the Bethel hills. The other company was under Jonathan at Gibeah in Benjamin. He sent the rest of the men home.
MSG.3: Jonathan attacked and killed the Philistine governor stationed at Geba (Gibeah). When the Philistines heard the news, they raised the alarm: "The Hebrews are in revolt!" Saul ordered the reveille trumpets blown throughout the land.
MSG.4: The word went out all over Israel, "Saul has killed the Philistine governor—drawn first blood! The Philistines are stirred up and mad as hornets!" Summoned, the army came to Saul at Gilgal.
MSG.5: The Philistines rallied their forces to fight Israel: three companies of chariots, six companies of cavalry, and so many infantry they looked like sand on the seashore. They went up into the hills and set up camp at Micmash, east of Beth Aven.
MSG.6: When the Israelites saw that they were way outnumbered and in deep trouble, they ran for cover, hiding in caves and pits, ravines and brambles and cisterns—wherever.
MSG.7: They retreated across the Jordan River, refugees fleeing to the country of Gad and Gilead. But Saul held his ground in Gilgal, his soldiers still with him but scared to death.
MSG.8: He waited seven days, the time set by Samuel. Samuel failed to show up at Gilgal, and the soldiers were slipping away, right and left.
MSG.9: So Saul took charge: "Bring me the burnt offering and the peace offerings!" He went ahead and sacrificed the burnt offering.
MSG.10: No sooner had he done it than Samuel showed up! Saul greeted him.
MSG.11:
Samuel said, "What on earth are you doing?"
Saul answered, "When I saw I was losing my army from under me, and that you hadn't come when you said you would, and that the Philistines were poised at Micmash,
MSG.12: I said, 'The Philistines are about to come down on me in Gilgal, and I haven't yet come before God asking for his help.' So I took things into my own hands, and sacrificed the burnt offering."
MSG.13: "That was a fool thing to do," Samuel said to Saul. "If you had kept the appointment that your God commanded, by now God would have set a firm and lasting foundation under your kingly rule over Israel.
MSG.14: As it is, your kingly rule is already falling to pieces. God is out looking for your replacement right now. This time he'll do the choosing. When he finds him, he'll appoint him leader of his people. And all because you didn't keep your appointment with God!"
MSG.15: At that, Samuel got up and left Gilgal. What army there was left followed Saul into battle. They went into the hills from Gilgal toward Gibeah in Benjamin. Saul looked over and assessed the soldiers still with him—a mere six hundred!
MSG.16: Saul, his son Jonathan, and the soldiers who had remained made camp at Geba (Gibeah) of Benjamin. The Philistines were camped at Micmash.
MSG.17: Three squads of raiding parties were regularly sent out from the Philistine camp. One squadron was assigned to the Ophrah road going toward Shual country;
MSG.18: another was assigned to the Beth Horon road; the third took the border road that rimmed the Valley of Hyenas.
MSG.19: There wasn't a blacksmith to be found anywhere in Israel. The Philistines made sure of that—"Lest those Hebrews start making swords and spears."
MSG.20: That meant that the Israelites had to go down among the Philistines to keep their farm tools—plowshares and mattocks, axes and sickles—sharp and in good repair.
MSG.21: They charged a silver coin for the plowshares and mattocks, and half that for the rest.
MSG.22: So when the battle of Micmash was joined, there wasn't a sword or spear to be found anywhere in Israel—except for Saul and his son Jonathan; they were both well-armed.
MSG.23: A patrol of Philistines took up a position at Micmash Pass.
